iron_rules: no interpolation; unverifiable cells excluded and disclosed
ranks and patterns only, no point estimates
method_notes: HPI rule: 2024 avg ÷ 2010 avg − 1 on BIS nominal quarterly (TW: Sinyi Q4/Q4)

Drawdown: two rules computed; headline = max drawdown in 2021Q1–2024Q4. The first rule (peak = max in 2021–2023 window) hid drawdowns for markets that recovered to new highs inside the window (AU); the switch is a window-artifact fix made before correlations were interpreted, both variants stored
Test 2 sample rule: numeric floating-rate stock shares only (IMF Table A5 + RBA + HKMA); JP variant excluded because BOJ never tightened in 2022–23, so the treatment was not applied

test1_money_vs_price.verdict: FAIL/WEAK: money variables alone do not rank 2010–2024 nominal house-price growth across the 12 markets (rho ≈ 0.15–0.22). Largest wrong-way points: MY (highest real rate, near-top price growth), KR (high M2, near-bottom growth), HK (lowest real rate, mid growth). Supports the framework only in its full form: money without the institutional/supply terms has no cross-sectional ranking power.

spearman_excl_JP.reason: BOJ did not tighten; natural experiment condition absent

test2_downside_stickiness.verdict: SUPPORTED (moderate): among markets that actually tightened, higher floating-rate share ranks with deeper 2021–24 nominal drawdowns (rho −0.68, n=7). MY annotation: predominantly floating yet max drawdown −0.2% — the institutional-stickiness residual (HDA, developer holding) the framework predicts.
